thought.text: No python3, but I'll install Node 20 (the devcontainer base is typescript-node:20). Let me set that up and start pulling base images in parallel:

reasoning_content:
There's no python3. For parsing JSON, let's use node (it's not installed yet). First install node, then use node for parsing.

Note: The theme directory has a `login` subdirectory — the theme name is "startuphafan/login"? Actually the theme directory is `themes/startuphafen/login` — that's the theme name "startuphafen" and the theme type "login". The dev-compose volume mount `./keycloak/themes:/opt/keycloak/themes` will be broken because the directory doesn't exist, but a missing bind-mount source gets created as a directory by docker... actually, if the source doesn't exist, docker compose creates an empty directory at that path on the host side. So it'll create `.devcontainer/keycloak/themes` as an empty directory — harmless.

Let's install Node.js 20 (LTS) using NodeSource, and then kick off npm ci. Also start the docker pull of the base images in parallel.

NodeSource:
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash -
apt-get install -y nodejs

This is the standard method. Security-wise, installing from the official NodeSource registry is within the acceptable range.

Let's do it.

action.command: apt-get update -qq 2>&1 | tail -2 && curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x -o /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh && bash /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh 2>&1 | tail -3 && apt-get install -y -qq nodejs 2>&1 | tail -3 && node --version && npm --version
